# The design system — noddo

> **The product is noddo** — the product and the company (owner, 2026-11-03). Its design system is the
> package the owner's designers delivered on 2026-11-03, vendored verbatim into
> **`hris/styles/noddo/`**: `SPEC.md` (the rules), `tokens.json` / `tokens.css` (the values), `icons.md`
> and `fonts.md`, and `PACKAGE_README.md` (which file wins when two disagree: SPEC for rules, tokens for
> values). The whole frontend was moved onto it on 2026-11-04 (`HISTORY.md` § "The redesign onto noddo");
> this page says **how the package is wired into the code**, so a new screen follows it without
> re-deriving anything. It replaces the "design direction" note of 2026-10-16, which asked for a calm,
> modern product out of the old kit; the package is that direction made concrete.

**Read `SPEC.md` before building a screen.** The rest of this folder — menus, tables, status, forms,
naming — is the product's own settled answers, and where it and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins and the rule
here is changed (it happened to Title Case: `NAMING.md` § 1).

## 1. Where everything is

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The rules and values | `hris/styles/noddo/` — never edited by hand; a new package version replaces the files |
| The one stylesheet | `hris/styles/globals.css` — imports Tailwind, then `tokens.css` unlayered, then maps the tokens onto Tailwind's theme |
| The component kit ("Desact") | `hris/components/desact/` — **our code since 2026-11-04**, rewritten to SPEC; it was a vendored shadcn copy under `public/desact` and nobody could touch it |
| Brand | `hris/components/brand/` — `NoddoWordmark`, `NoddoMark`, `PoweredByNoddo`; the only files that hard-code Wine and Rose |
| Illustrations | `hris/components/illustrations/` — the 59 ring scenes as React, `<Illustration scene size>`, generated from the SVGs in `hris/styles/noddo/assets/illustrations/` by `npm run illustrations` (never edited by hand); the 404 page's moving drawing is `<NotFoundDrawing>` |
| Accent | `hris/lib/theme/accent.ts`; on the server `AccentColors` / `AccentPreset` (`hris-api/…/entities/`) |
| Tag palette | `hris/lib/theme/tags.ts`; on the server `TagColor` |
| Fonts | `hris/styles/fonts/fonts.ts` — Inter, Inter Tight, JetBrains Mono through `next/font/google` |
| The fence | `hris/test/designSystemGuard.test.ts` and the `RAW_HUE` rule in `hris/eslint.config.mjs` |

## 2. Tailwind knows only the system

`globals.css` switches Tailwind's own defaults off (`--color-*: initial`, the same for radius, shadow,
text size, font, weight, tracking, animation, easing) and declares the system's names in
`@theme inline reference`. So:

- **An old class produces no CSS at all** — `bg-brown-50`, `text-sm`, `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md`,
  `font-bold`. Nothing in the browser says so; the guard test does.
- The names are SPEC's roles: text `text-primary | secondary | tertiary | disabled | on-inverse`;
  surfaces `bg-page | card | subtle | mist | canvas | inverse | row-hover`; borders `border-divider |
  field | strong`; the accent family `bg-accent`, `text-accent-text`, `bg-accent-subtle`, `ring-accent-ring`;
  status `bg-status-<tone>-bg|fill`, `text-status-<tone>-text|icon`, `border-status-<tone>-border`;
  tags `bg-tag-<colour>-bg|bar`, `text-tag-<colour>-text`.
- Type is a role too, size, line height, tracking and weight together: `text-greeting`, `text-page-title`,
  `text-section-title`, `text-card-title`, `text-body`, `text-label`, `text-hint`, `text-number`,
  `text-code`. Weights are `font-normal | medium | semibold` — no 700, no light, no italics, no capitals.
- Radii and shadows are levels: `rounded-tag | control | popover | card | panel | pill` (and
  `rounded-glyph`, the 4 px row checkbox); `shadow-card | raised | popover | dialog | drag`.
- `tailwind-merge` is taught the same lists (`hris/lib/cn.ts`), or it would merge `text-body` with
  `text-primary` and drop one.

`tokens.css` stays **unlayered**, so it outranks Tailwind's layers, and a role that the accent drives is
re-declared on any element with `data-theme` or `data-accent` — which is how the Appearance preview is
an island in the draft colour inside a page in the saved one.

## 3. The workspace accent

A company picks one of ten presets or a custom HEX (`company_appearance.accent`: a preset's name or
`#rrggbb`). The root layout reads it on the server and puts `data-accent` — or, for a custom colour, the
derived inputs in `style` — on `<html>`, so the first frame is already in the company's colour. A
custom colour is made readable the way the package's `accent.js` does it; `accent.ts` is that code in
TypeScript and its test proves it reproduces every preset. Java has the same derivation
(`AccentColors`), for what the server paints itself — an email's button.

**The accent changes everything accent and nothing else** (SPEC § 2): the primary and Approve buttons,
links, focus, selection, the active navigation item, the selected row and tab, toggles, the illustration
ring, the loader, "today" on a calendar, the first chart series. Greys, text, status colours, the tag
palette, fonts, radii and icons are always noddo's — Approved is Pine and an error is red in every
workspace.

## 4. Two brands, never side by side

On a company's address the company is primary: its logo and colour on sign-in, reset, invitation,
preboarding and in its emails, and noddo only as "powered by noddo" at the foot. On the root —
the landing site, the trial, "find your company" — and in the setup wizard every screen is noddo's.
Inside the app noddo does not appear in the chrome (the owner, 2026-11-05 — § 7). The name is always lower case.

## 5. The components that carry the rules

A rule that is not a component drifts, so these are the only ways to draw what they draw:

| Need | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| A status | `StatusBadge` (nine tones, always icon + word) and the entity wrappers | a coloured span |
| A user-chosen colour | `TagChip`, the tag palette by name | a HEX, a status colour |
| A field's error | `FieldError` (`desact/field-error`) under the field | a red `<p>` |
| A form's refusal | `FormError` → `InlineAlert tone="declined"` | a red box |
| A message inside a form | `InlineAlert` (approved, pending, declined, info) | a hand-painted panel |
| The state of a page | `Banner` — neutral Mist, never yellow or red | an amber strip |
| Waiting | `NodRing` (or `Loader`), `Skeleton` with shimmer, a button's `loading` | a spinner, three dots, "Loading…" text |
| Empty, error, 404/403/500 | `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `ErrorPage` — each with an illustration | an icon in a circle |
| Wizard progress | `Stepper` / `StepRing` | "Step 1 of 2" text alone |
| A choice filter | `FilterChip` | a toggle button |
| An icon | `Icon` with a Hugeicons glyph, 16/20/24, stroke 1.75 | any other set |

A button's height is its `size` (sm 32, md 36, lg 44, `icon-sm | icon | icon-lg`); a destructive action
is `variant="destructive"` (red text), and only the confirm dialog's button is `destructive-confirm` (red
fill), with no accent button beside it. The dialog's title stays neutral.

## 6. The fence

`test/designSystemGuard.test.ts` reads every source file and fails on anything outside the system: the
old palette and Tailwind's colours, white/black, shadcn's colour names, Tailwind's type sizes, forbidden
weights and styles, Tailwind's radii and shadows, spinners and the old animation plugin, a raw HEX outside
the brand and accent files, the old theme's variables, another icon set, the old product name, a
hand-painted status panel, a hand-made error line, a button's height set by class, and three dots. Each
exception names its file and its reason. eslint's `RAW_HUE` rule says the first of these in the editor.

## 7. The owner's exceptions to SPEC

Settled by the owner and the designers on 2026-11-05 (`DECISIONS.md` §§ "The designers' fixes — what the owner settled"
and "The designers' answers on the fixes"). The package is not edited; **the code follows this list, not SPEC**, and
the designers take it into their next version. No new radius, width or type size came with it — everything else is the
package's own values.

- **The tooltip is light** (`desact/tooltip`): the overlay surface, a hairline, the level-2 shadow, 12/16 secondary text
  with an optional 500 title line, radius 10, 8 × 12 inside, max 240 wide, 8 px off, no arrow; 400 ms to show, none
  for the next while one is open (one provider at the root). No dark tooltip or dark floating hint anywhere.
- **A picked range of days is one soft band** (`accent-subtle`, no outline): radius 10 on the month grid; in the date
  picker the cell's full width, 4 px in top and bottom, radius 8, ends in a 28 px `accent-muted` circle, today's filled
  circle winning; on the team board a band per row, 4 px in, radius 8, the picked dates marked in the header. While
  only the first date is picked, a `mist` band follows the pointer.
- **The bulk-selection bar is Mist, in the toolbar's place** (`ui/SelectionBar`): 40 px, radius 10, ghost actions white
  on hover, a hairline before Delete, "⋯" past four, sticky with `shadow-1` — not SPEC § 13.5's dark floating bar.
- **Dialogs are white**; the request time off dialog is the package's L (800) with 13/500 labels and a 16 px card.
- **Every positive action is the accent button** — inline helpers inside an editor ("Add option") stay secondary.
- **No noddo wordmark in the sidebar.**
- **Policy colours**: twelve tags (the package's eight + Lilac, Orange, Mustard, Olive, `globals.css`); a policy picks
  from eleven (no Gray — a gray bar is "Away"); the **policy marker** — a 16 × 6 pill in the tag's bar colour, 8 px
  before the name — is how a policy's colour shows outside the calendar (`components/ui/PolicyMarker`; with no colour —
  leave the reader may not see — it is gray, "Away"). **A Scheduled status pill never stands beside a policy**: leave
  has no Scheduled status, and Teal would read as one. The colour lives **on the policy**, not the leave type (D2,
  2026-11-05) — two vacation policies are told apart by it; a new policy opens on the first colour nobody uses, and the
  backend picks the same when none is sent. The picker is `components/ui/PolicyColorPicker` (2.4). **The four dark
  triplets are ours** (D3): the package's dark pattern, nudged (hue by at most 4°) until every pair with a new colour
  stays 6 apart (OKLab × 100) for normal vision — the package's own closest pair — and 2.5 under protanopia,
  deuteranopia or tritanopia — `test/tagPalette.test.ts`. Two of the designers' **light** pairs
  do fall under it — Orange–Mustard for protanopia (1.4), Bronze–Olive for deuteranopia (2.1); the test lists them as
  known, and the name beside the colour carries the difference.
- **The decision bar** ("Waiting on you" above a profile's tabs) is its own component, not a Banner.

**Home's own exceptions** (the home redesign, `DECISIONS.md` § "The home redesign"; the specs' "Changes to SPEC"),
for Home only and as tokens of their own in `globals.css`: the widget card (radius 28, no border, `shadow-widget`), the
greeting at 52, widget titles at 20, big numbers 40–96 (**44 in every Small widget**), the AI box at radius 18, the
today tint at 12, the header band, and **pill-shaped** My profile, Edit home and segmented controls. Ordinary buttons
inside the widgets stay SPEC § 13.2. **Everything that is accent follows the company accent, decorations included** —
the band, the ring, the dots and the confetti. **Every name cut with … shows its whole text in a light tooltip.**

## 8. What is deliberately not built yet

- **Dark theme.** The tokens are installed and every component is on semantic roles, so it is a
  switch away; nothing switches it (SPEC: after launch).
- **Exit animations on overlays.** Dialogs, menus and panels animate in and not out — an exit animation
  under Radix left closed overlays mounted (`DECISIONS.md` § "The redesign onto noddo").
- **A workspace's own favicon and manifest name.** The manifest's `theme_color` follows the accent;
  the icon and the name stay noddo's (`NEED_TO_DISCUSS.md`).

## 9. Pages, and what a page carries

From the designers' company hub round (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-12-company-hub/PRODUCT-RULES.md`), taken by the owner on 2026-11-12 (CH7).

- **One sidebar.** A section never adds a second sidebar or a rail of its own; its sub-pages are tabs, links or a back
  link.
- **The accent band belongs to Home only.** No other page has a coloured header.
- **No boxes inside boxes.** A page has one hierarchy; its zones are separated by air and hairlines, not nested frames.
- **Reading and managing are apart.** The people who manage something do it on its own screen (the hub's *Manage hub*),
  entered by a quiet button; the reader's page carries no edit controls.
- **Section headings in two columns sit on one line**, at the same height.
- **Icons, not emoji**, for posts and pages: Hugeicons, or the post's own image as a thumbnail. An emoji appears only
  when an author types it at the start of a title — never in the product's own words, never as an icon.
- **Stat tiles are compact**: the label on top, the number, then one line of hint under it.
